Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: People are not what they seem
The world is a dangerous place

issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together' directly conflicts with 'I can talk about what happened very easily.' For a severe mugging-related PTSD profile, markedly fragmented recall and very easy verbal access to the trauma narrative are hard to reconcile as describing the same current memory presentation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The Memory node is internally incoherent for a severe mugging/robbery PTSD presentation: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' suggests low avoidance and relatively integrated, verbally accessible trauma memory, whereas simultaneously endorsing very vivid detailed recall and body-based painful reliving implies a highly sensory, distressing, poorly integrated trauma memory. This combination is possible in milder cases, but here it is hard to reconcile clinically within the same Memory profile. The Negative Appraisals items are coherent for robbery trauma, but the Memory selections do not fit cleanly with that node pattern or with the strong Negative Appraisals ↔ Memory linkage in the formulation.

issues.item: Constant Vigilance: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next
issues.explanation: This item is more characteristic of ongoing threat/safety behavior than of a pure negative appraisal. In this profile, Threat is not endorsed and all Threat-related edges are inactive, while the active formulation is specifically centered on a Memory ↔ Negative Appraisals loop. The mistrust items fit robbery-related appraisals, but 'Constant Vigilance' introduces a prominent current-threat theme that is not supported elsewhere in the profile.

vignette: Rohan's eyes would often glaze over as he methodically cleaned the hotel rooms, his mind wandering back to that fateful evening two years ago. He had just finished a double shift at work and was walking home from the bus stop when three men approached him, their faces obscured by hoods. The memory still seared his brain like a branding iron - the feeling of being pinned against the wall, the sound of his wallet chain snapping as it was ripped from his neck, and the pain that coursed through his jaw as he was punched in the face. Even now, when the memory returned, Rohan's body would react as if it were happening all over again - his jaw ached, his temples throbbed, and his chest tightened. The vividness of the memory still unsettled him. He remembered every detail: the way the streetlights cast long shadows on the sidewalk, the smell of garbage from the nearby dumpster, and the sound of laughter from one of his attackers as he lay helpless on the ground. Rohan often struggled to articulate what had happened that night; he knew the sequence of events, but putting it into words seemed impossible. His wife, Leela, would try to get him to talk about it, but he'd shake his head, feeling like a failure for not being able to describe something so pivotal. The mugging had left Rohan with a deep-seated mistrust of others. He now believed that people wore masks to conceal their true intentions. As he cleaned the hotel rooms, he couldn't help but wonder what secrets guests were hiding behind closed doors. His colleagues at work noticed a change in him too - he was more reserved and no longer participated in conversations during breaks. Rohan felt like he was walking on eggshells, constantly anticipating the next potential threat. His perception of the world had also shifted; to him, it now seemed like a treacherous place where anyone could be a predator. Simple tasks like taking public transportation or walking alone at night filled him with anxiety. Leela tried to reassure him that he was safe, but Rohan couldn't shake off the feeling that danger lurked around every corner. As time passed, Rohan's avoidance behaviors became more pronounced. He stopped taking the bus and instead opted for a longer walk home from work, choosing routes that were better lit. He also turned down social invitations, preferring to stay at home with Leela rather than venture out into what he saw as an uncertain world. His job performance suffered too - guests would complain about uncleaned rooms or forgotten towels, and Rohan's manager began to notice his lack of attention to detail. Leela grew concerned about Rohan's increasing isolation and encouraged him to seek help. It wasn't until they had a heart-to-heart conversation on the eve of their wedding anniversary that Rohan finally agreed to see a therapist. As he sat in the waiting room, filling out paperwork, Rohan couldn't help but think about what his life would be like if he could just shake off these lingering fears and mistrusts. He was tired of living in a state of constant vigilance, tired of feeling like an outsider in his own world.
